answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grant grading and voting weight only through earned, non-transferable reputation. Each new key starts as a hollow account with zero weight. Per epoch it can earn one point, and only if five random established jurors pass its fresh answer; duplicates are rejected. Points sit in an ivory ledger bound to that key, never sold or merged, under a velvet cap of 30. So 100 fakes need 100 distinct passing answers each epoch, and splitting one writer's output across keys adds nothing. Weakness: a farm of real writers still grows, only slowly.
